summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The four calls stay neutral with low conviction; all four pass every setup check, which in the base rates meant nothing. Nothing here is expected to beat the index or is something to buy; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: All four of the brain's runners look fit today. But in old races, the fit-looking runners did no better than names pulled from a hat, so the brain keeps watching with pretend money. The family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing changes. The weekly buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual for money we will leave alone for years, and money we may need soon stays safe. The market has gone sideways again; that is ordinary.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stands at one week won and one lost, and this week's bet is a little ahead so far. Luck alone wins about half the weeks, so this means nothing yet.

Third, a lesson. Today all four names we watch pass every one of our setup checks. That sounds like a strong signal, yet in our own history names with a perfect score did no better than the rest. A full set of green lights is still not a map of the road ahead.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Microsoft's report was due around the latest close, so how the market took it is not in our data yet. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
